newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh seen ready to try Mujib killers.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh seen ready to try Mujib killers.

text.p: Bangladesh is moving to bring the suspected killers of the country's independence leader to trial after his daughter, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, vowed to bring them to justice, officials said on Saturday.

"The stage (for the trial) is set. The trial would begin almost immediately after parliament clears a legal barrier to the prosecution of those who killed Sheikh Mujibur Rahman," one official, who declined to be identified, said.
Sheikh Hasina's 10-year-old brother Sheikh Russel was killed along with his parents, two brothers and several relatives, in Bangladesh's first military coup on August 15, 1975.
Six army officers, suspected masterminds of the coup, were later assigned to diplomatic jobs abroad by Mujib's successors.

The legal barrier to the trial centres on the success of a law commission Hasina created. The panel has recommended that a 1975 ordinance that gave the coup leaders and accomplices indemnity from prosecution can be overruled by a simple majority vote in parliament, which could be taken in a matter of weeks.
Hasina's Awami League has a majority in the 330-member legislature, which begins its autumn session on November 1.
"The indemnity ordinance is expected to be repealed in the next session and the trial will follow soon," one Awami leader said.
On Friday, Hasina told a memorial service for her brother Sheikh Russel that "the killers shall be tried and punished.
"Law will come down heavily on those who had orphaned me...and deprived the nation of its founding father."
All six suspects have absconded since Hasina, who took over as Prime Minister after general elections in June, announced plans to hunt down her father's killers.
Hasina's government has urged all countries not to grant political asylum or shelter to the accused killers. As yet, Dhaka has been unable to bring any of them back, officials said on Saturday.
The government was now planning to seek the help of Interpol to track them down and arrange their extradition.
One suspected killer was reported to be in Bangkok. But Dhaka does not have an extradition treaty with Thai government, officials said.
"We don't have any idea so far where the others may be sheltering now. We are trying to locate them," one official said.
Bangladesh police have already arrested three former army officers as well as Mujib's information minister, Taheruddin Thakur, as part of the murder investigation.
The officers are retired colonels Farook Reehman and Shahriar Rashid Khan and retired major Mohammad Khairuzzaman.
They are also suspects in the killing of four top Awami leaders in Dhaka Central Jail in November, 1975.
Police said on Saturday they had also detained "several low-rank former army men" believed to be involved in the 1975 coup.
"They are divulging sensitive and important information," one police officer told reporters, but gave no more details.
